speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, how old is the infant, and when did these episodes of stridor and wheezing first begin? Also, do you notice the symptoms occurring specifically when the baby is feeding or crying?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Tracheomalacia. The combination of recurrent stridor and wheezing that worsens with crying, feeding, and neck flexion, along with post-tussive or post-prandial vomiting, is highly characteristic of dynamic airway collapse due to tracheomalacia.
